triggers: how do I connect to wifi
how do I join a wireless network
how to connect to a wifi network from the terminal
what's the command to connect to wifi
how do I get online over wifi
how do I see available wifi networks
answer:
InterGenOS uses **NetworkManager**, so the CLI is `nmcli` (or the menu UI `nmtui`):

```
nmcli device wifi list                          # scan for networks
nmcli device wifi connect '<SSID>' password '<password>'
```

For an interactive menu instead, just run `nmtui` and pick "Activate a connection". On the desktop, use the network icon in the top-right. Saved networks reconnect automatically.

triggers: how do I check my network connection
how do I see my ip address
how do I check if I'm online
how to see network status
what's the command to show my ip
how do I list network connections
answer:
Check connectivity and addresses:

```
nmcli device status            # each interface and whether it's connected
nmcli connection show          # saved/active connections
ip addr                        # all interface IP addresses
ping -c3 1.1.1.1               # is the network actually reachable?
```

`nmcli device status` is the quickest "am I connected?" check; `ping` a known host to confirm traffic actually flows (vs. just having an address).

triggers: how do I check the firewall
how do I open a port
how do I see firewall rules
how to configure the firewall
what firewall does InterGenOS use
how do I allow incoming connections
how do I use iptables
iptables command
does InterGenOS use iptables
answer:
InterGenOS ships an **nftables** firewall with a default-deny inbound policy. Inspect the live ruleset:

```
sudo nft list ruleset
```

The defaults live in `/etc/intergenos-firewall-defaults/`. Outbound traffic is allowed; new inbound connections are dropped unless a rule permits them. Opening a port means adding an nft rule — do this deliberately, since every opened port widens the attack surface. For a service you installed, prefer binding it to localhost where possible rather than opening the firewall.

If you know iptables: it is present for compatibility (NetworkManager consumes it), but **nft is the native interface** on InterGenOS — write any rule you add by hand as an nft rule, and read the live state with `nft list ruleset` rather than `iptables -L`.

triggers: how do I change my dns
how do I fix dns resolution
how do I test dns
how to set a dns server
what's wrong with my dns
how do I look up a hostname
answer:
DNS is managed through NetworkManager. Test resolution and set servers:

```
resolvectl query example.com        # does a name resolve?
resolvectl status                   # current DNS servers per link
# set DNS for a saved connection (persists):
nmcli connection modify '<name>' ipv4.dns '1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9'
nmcli connection up '<name>'        # re-apply
```

If names won't resolve but `ping 1.1.1.1` works, it's DNS — point the connection at a known resolver as above and bring it back up.

triggers: why won't my wifi connect
answer:
```
nmcli radio wifi                    # is Wi-Fi enabled? (should say 'enabled')
nmcli device status                 # is the wifi device 'connected' or 'disconnected'?
nmcli device wifi list              # does your SSID appear? (weak signal / wrong band?)
nmcli connection up "SSID"          # retry the saved connection
journalctl -u NetworkManager -b --no-pager | tail -40   # recent NM errors (auth failures show here)
```
Common causes: wrong password (re-run `nmcli device wifi connect ... password ...`), Wi-Fi radio off
(`nmcli radio wifi on`), or driver/firmware — `linux-firmware` and `wireless-regdb` ship, so most adapters work.

triggers: why is my wifi not working
answer:
```
nmcli device status                 # is a wifi device present and what state is it in?
nmcli radio wifi on                 # turn the radio on if it's off
rfkill list                         # is wifi blocked in hardware/software? (util-linux)
systemctl status NetworkManager     # is the network service running?
```
If no wifi device appears at all, it's likely a driver/firmware gap — capture `lspci -k | grep -iA3 network`
and ask InterGen to look at the adapter.

triggers: why can't I resolve domain names
answer:
```
ping -c1 1.1.1.1                   # if this works but names don't, it's a DNS problem
getent hosts intergenos.org       # test name resolution directly (no dig/nslookup on InterGenOS)
resolvectl status                  # show the active DNS servers (systemd-resolved)
nmcli device show | grep IP4.DNS  # which DNS servers NetworkManager handed out
```
Note: InterGenOS does not ship `dig`/`nslookup`/`host` — use `getent hosts <name>` or `ping <name>` to test
resolution, and `resolvectl` / `nmcli` to inspect the DNS servers.

triggers: how do I change my DNS server
answer:
```
# Set DNS on the active NetworkManager connection (persists):
nmcli connection modify "<connection-name>" ipv4.dns "1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1"
nmcli connection modify "<connection-name>" ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes
nmcli connection up "<connection-name>"      # re-activate to apply
# find <connection-name> with:  nmcli connection show
# GUI: Settings -> Network/Wi-Fi -> gear icon -> IPv4 -> DNS (turn Automatic off, enter servers).
```

triggers: how do I ssh into another machine
answer:
```
ssh user@host                      # e.g. ssh alice@192.168.1.20  (openssh is shipped)
ssh -p 2222 user@host              # non-default port
ssh-keygen -t ed25519              # first set up a key (recommended over passwords)

```

triggers: how do I copy a file to another computer
answer:
```
scp file.txt user@host:/path/          # copy one file over SSH (openssh)
scp -r folder/ user@host:/path/        # copy a folder
# for large / repeated transfers, rsync (shipped) is better:
rsync -avP folder/ user@host:/path/
```

triggers: how do I mount a usb drive
answer:
```
Desktop: just plug it in — it auto-mounts (udisks2/gvfs) and appears in Files (Nautilus) in the sidebar.
  Click the eject icon in Files to safely remove it.
Terminal:
  lsblk                              # find the device, e.g. /dev/sdb1
  udisksctl mount -b /dev/sdb1       # mount via udisks (no sudo, mounts under /run/media/$USER/)
  udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sdb1     # unmount when done
```

triggers: why won't my printer print
answer:
```
Settings -> Printers: is the printer shown and NOT paused? (resume it if paused).
Terminal:
  lpstat -p -d           # printer state + default printer (CUPS)
  lpstat -o              # stuck jobs in the queue
  cancel -a              # clear all queued jobs, then try again
  systemctl status cups  # is the print service running?
```
Common causes: printer paused, a jammed job blocking the queue, wrong default printer, or the printer offline
(check power/network). InterGenOS uses CUPS — the Settings > Printers panel is the primary control.

triggers: are there printers configured on this laptop
what printers do I have
list my printers
show my printers
is a printer set up
which printers are installed
answer:
InterGenOS uses **CUPS** for printing, so you can list what's configured from the terminal:
```
lpstat -p -d           # each printer and its state, plus the default printer
lpstat -v              # each printer's connection (USB / network URI)
lpstat -o              # any jobs currently in the queue
```
If `lpstat -p` prints nothing, no printers are configured yet — add one from **Settings → Printers**. The GNOME **Settings → Printers** panel shows the same list in a window.
